title: Meet and Greet
subtitle: From the Alpha Strike box · 4 vs 2 · about 60 minutes
coachNotes: The Alpha Strike box’s own first scenario (Quick-Start Rulebook p. 26). A lance of Northwind Highlanders meets two Clan Jade Falcon scouts.
Side A has four Inner Sphere ’Mechs. Side B has two Clan OmniMechs with better pilots, so it is outnumbered but not outgunned.
New: better pilots. Skill is the base to-hit number, so a Skill 2 pilot hits on 2 less than a Skill 4 one. Better pilots cost more Point Value, which is why the two sides’ totals look uneven.

New: heat attacks (HT). The Pouncer’s HT1/1/- means a hit at short or medium range also gives the target 1 heat at Clean up (the End Phase). A ’Mech takes at most 2 heat a turn this way, and it lands even if the target didn’t fire.
Forced Withdrawal is on, as in Full Lances: crippled ’Mechs head home, and leaving the table counts as destroyed.
tableSteps: Use an open table about 3 feet across. Measure in inches and ignore printed hexes.

Woods: each player takes four single trees. Side B places first, then take turns, each within 24 inches of the centre of the table. Each player puts three of their trees within 4 inches of each other to make a patch of woods. No other piece goes within 4 inches of another.
Each side’s own long table edge is its home edge. A crippled ’Mech must head back toward it.
Side A places two ’Mechs, at least 20 inches from the centre toward its edge. Then Side B places one the same way. Repeat, two for one, until all six are down.
Side B’s Nova and Pouncer are Clan OmniMechs. If you own the Alpha Strike box, their cards are in it; the app has the numbers too.
winningSummary: Cripple or destroy every enemy ’Mech. A ’Mech that leaves the table counts as destroyed. The book has no turn limit; the app stops at 10 turns, and then the side with more Structure left wins.
